title: 2019 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: Let \(S\) be the set of all positive integer divisors of \(100{,}000.\) How many numbers are the product of two distinct elements of \(S?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(100{,}000=2^5\cdot5^5,\) every divisor is \(2^a5^b\) with \(0\le a,b\le5.\) A product of two divisors is \(2^x5^y\) with \(0\le x,y\le10,\) and every such pair \((x,y)\) is attainable, giving \(11\cdot11=121\) values.

We need two distinct divisors. A value \(2^x5^y\) is forced to be a divisor times itself only when both \(x\) and \(y\) have a unique split, which happens exactly when \(x,y\in\{0,10\}.\) Those \(4\) corner values (\(1,\ 2^{10},\ 5^{10},\ 2^{10}5^{10}\)) cannot use two distinct divisors.

The count is \(121-4=117.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Divisors are \(2^a5^b\) with \(0\le a,b\le5;\) products are \(2^x5^y\) with \(0\le x,y\le10\)
All \(11\times11\) products arise; discard those obtainable only as a divisor times itself
